主要内容: Peloton, a fitness equipment company known for its at-home fitness cycles and treadmills, revealed its financials for the first time in its IPO filing. The company reported a 110% increase in sales to $915 million for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019, compared to $435 million in fiscal 2018. However, its net loss widened to $245.7 million, up from $47.9 million in the prior year. Peloton plans to raise $500 million in its IPO and expand its international presence, which it expects to bring new costs. The company also disclosed it will sell Class B stock, granting 20 votes per share. Peloton's connected fitness subscriber base grew to 511,202 in 2019, up from 245,667 a year earlier. It also reported a 95% retention rate for its connected fitness subscribers since fiscal 2016. Peloton has expanded its product line beyond its $2,000 bicycles to include treadmills priced at $3,995 and introduced digital memberships for $19.49 per month, targeting users who may not want to invest in its equipment. The company also warned about the complexities of its music license agreements, which could impact its operations. Peloton, which will list under the ticker PTON, expects to trade its shares on Nasdaq. The company has faced several legal challenges, including lawsuits from artists like Lady Gaga and Drake over the use of their music without permission, and litigation with competitor Flywheel over patent infringement. Peloton warned that its use of third-party content may be subject to claims of infringement or misappropriation. Additionally, the company identified material weaknesses in its internal control over financial reporting, which it has not fully addressed as of June 30. To address these issues, it plans to add more qualified personnel. Peloton is working with underwriters including Goldman Sachs & Co and J.P. Morgan. The company is also noted for its presence on CNBC's "Disruptor 50" list for the past two years.
